Figure 12.25: Leaving an organization
When a B2B user leaves the organization, the user's account is deleted from the directory and
placed in the Deleted users area. It remains there for 30 days, during which the administrator
can recover idx_e9960f91 the user's account if required. If the account is not restored within 30 days, it is
permanently deleted. Data deletion can take an additional 30 days.
Best practices
Effective management idx_be226319 of guest users starts with treating every external identity as a
temporary, high-variance access point that must be governed with clarity, constraint, and
continuous review. Following are some best practices to manage B2B guests in the workforce
tenant.
Configure the most restrictive external collaboration settings as per the organization's
requirements.
Enable automatic redemption only for trusted partner organizations.
Enforce least privilege for guest users.
Disable guest ability to enumerate directory objects.
Create guest-specific Conditional Access policies that enforce MFA and location
restrictions.
Perform periodic access reviews for guest accounts to review guest access to resources
and inactive guest accounts.
Use access packages to provide birthright access to guests. Configure expiration on
access packages.
Implement Terms of Use for external users.
Use cross-tenant access settings for collaboration with partner organizations.
Use federation for guest users. Avoid creating accounts for guests in your tenant.

Strong guest governance isn't a one-time setup. It is a continuous discipline that keeps your
tenant secure, predictable, and collaboration-ready through every external identity lifecycle.
Pricing
Entra External ID is idx_b88ad335 billed based on Monthly Active Users (MAU). It offers idx_d27b3493 the first 50,000
MAU for free. Each user who authenticates to the tenant once a month contributes to the MAU.
Ensure that there is an Azure subscription attached to your Microsoft Entra ID tenant for
billing purposes.
Summary
This chapter began by introducing Microsoft Entra External ID and clarifying the differences
between workforce and external tenant setups. It also covered how External ID functions
within a workforce tenant. You learned how to invite and manage guest users, set up external
collaboration for B2B scenarios, and adjust both default and organization-specific cross-tenant
access settings for direct B2B connections and multi-cloud environments. The chapter
discussed enabling synchronization between tenants and clouds, outlined the different
identity providers for B2B collaboration, and described ways to secure and govern B2B users.
The following chapter will explore the CIAM features of Entra ID.

Tenants
Consumer Identity and Access Management (CIAM) is a specialized branch of identity
management focused on providing secure, seamless, and user-friendly digital experiences for
external idx_7af9e992 users, such as customers, partners, or citizens. Unlike traditional workforce identity
solutions, which manage internal employee access, CIAM solutions are designed to handle the
unique challenges of managing large numbers of external users who often interact with an
organization through web portals, mobile apps, and other digital services.
At its core, CIAM enables organizations to authenticate, authorize, and manage the identities
of their consumers while protecting sensitive information and complying with privacy
regulations. Key capabilities typically include self-service registration, social login integration,
multi-factor authentication (MFA), consent management, and robust data privacy controls.
These features help organizations deliver personalized experiences, foster customer trust, and
ensure security without introducing unnecessary friction.
As digital engagement becomes a critical business driver, CIAM platforms must scale to
support millions of users and provide high availability. They must also integrate with
marketing, analytics, and customer service systems to deliver unified, omnichannel
experiences. Ultimately, a well-implemented CIAM solution not only safeguards user data but
also helps organizations build lasting relationships and drive business growth.
This chapter will cover
External ID in the external tenant
Create an external tenant
Configure applications for SSO
•

Create and customize user journeys
Securing external tenants
Migrating to Entra External ID
External ID in external tenants
In addition to B2B collaboration, Microsoft Entra External ID also includes Microsoft's next
generation CIAM solution that enables businesses to make their applications available to
consumers idx_76ab9feb and business customers, leveraging features like self-service registration,
personalized sign-in experiences and customer account management. These CIAM features are
built on Microsoft Entra ID enabling organizations to benefit from platform features like
security, scalability and compliance.
External ID in external tenants is a separate directory from your workforce tenant which is
used by employees and for B2B collaboration. The first step toward enabling external ID for
consumers is to create an external tenant. This way you create a distinct tenant that follows the
Microsoft Entra model but is configured for consumer scenarios. This external tenant consists
of
A directory: This is the location where the consumer identities are stored.
Applications: To make applications available to consumers, they must be registered

with Microsoft Entra ID so that it can perform identity and access management idx_a4ab57d1 for
those applications. Applications idx_adfb2d01 that use Security Assertion Markup Language
(SAML) or OpenID Connect (OIDC) can be registered in the external tenant.
User flows: Administrators can enable self-service sign-up, sign-in, and password
reset experiences for consumers.
Extensions: Custom authentication extensions can be used if user attributes or data
from external systems need to be added.
Sign-in methods: Entra External ID offers various sign-in methods like email and
password, email and OTP, social IdPs and custom OIDC providers.
Encryption keys: Using Entra External ID application owners can add and manage
encryption keys for signing and validating tokens, client secrets, certificates and
passwords.
Entra External idx_fc991ba9 ID is billed based on Monthly Active Users (MAU).

Configuring identity providers
Just like idx_136d14ab in the workforce tenant, external ID in the external tenant offers several ways in which
users can sign up. The following options are available:
Email and password
This option is enabled by default. With this option, users can sign up with their email address
and password. This creates a local account in the external tenant and the user's password is
stored in idx_df13aa70 the external tenant directory. The user clicks on the No account? Create one option
on the login screen. They can enter any existing email address. They are then sent an OTP to
confirm the email address. Once they enter the OTP, they are asked to choose a password. On
subsequent logins, the user uses the password they selected during the sign-up process. The
following screenshot shows the user's journey when signing up with email and password.

Later, if the user forgets their password, they can reset it using the Forgot password? link on
the password page.

Using this idx_83794995 option, users can sign up using an email address and an OTP. They are not required
to create a password. They receive an OTP each time they sign in.

In some scenarios, organizations want the users to be able to sign in using a username. This
could be idx_4430ab7b a frequent flyer number, loyalty number, student ID, etc. With this option, users can
choose to log in using a username or their email address. To enable username as a sign-in
identifier, it must be enabled in Microsoft Entra admin center. Following are the steps:

navigate to Entra ID | External Identities | Sign-in identifiers.

Social identities
When users sign in to different applications, they must create user accounts specific to those
applications. This leads to bad password practices like repeating passwords across
applications. This is prone to credential stuffing attacks. Administrators also must maintain
passwords idx_f980e239 for users, making them responsible for protecting identities from password spray
and brute force attacks. Federation solves this problem by passing the responsibility of user
authentication to an external IdP. External ID in external tenant supports federation with
Google, Facebook, and Apple. When social identity federation is enabled, users get the option
to sign-in using that identity on the sign-in and sign-up page as shown below:

Federation with a custom OpenID Connect IdP allows users to sign up and sign in using

navigate to Entra ID | External Identities | All identity providers.

discovery URI for your IdP.
Issuer URI: This is the entity of your IdP that issues access tokens for the
applications.
Client ID: This idx_69606c7d is the identifier your IdP uses to identify the registered
application.
Client authentication: This is the type of authentication method used to
authenticate to your IdP using the token endpoint. The available options are
client_secret: If this option is selected, the client secret must be
provided.
private_key_jwt: If this option is selected, the public key needs to be
provided in the OpenID provider metadata.
Scope: This is the information and permissions required from the IdP.
Response type: This describes the information that is sent back in the initial call

Following are the steps to set up SAML/WS-Fed IdP federation:

https://tailspintoys.com.au, then they must add a TXT record to their domain's
DNS in the following format:
tailspintoys.com. IN TXT DirectFedAuthUrl=https://
tailspingroup.com

For users to be able to access your application, you must register your application with Entra
ID. Registering idx_ee38e363 the application with Entra External ID creates a unidirectional trust
relationship between your application and Entra External ID. The application trusts Entra
External ID and not the other way around. Once the application object is created, it cannot be
moved to another tenant.

option makes your multitenant app available for users in any Microsoft Entra
tenant and Microsoft personal accounts.

Custom authentication extensions
Custom authentication extensions in Entra External ID allow organizations to tailor the
authentication idx_7ccaa0eb experience to meet unique business or security requirements. By leveraging
these extensions, you can integrate external systems, apply advanced validation logic, or
trigger custom workflows during the sign-in process. This flexibility is particularly useful for
scenarios where out-of-the-box authentication methods are insufficient. Developers can create
and register their own RESTful API endpoints to interact with Entra ID during authentication,
enabling dynamic user validation, step-up authentication, or integration with third-party

Microsoft Entra External ID offers the following custom authentication extensions.
OnAttributeCollectionStart: Using this extension developers can modify the sign-up
experience for customers. The OnAttributeCollectionStart event occurs before the
attribute collection page renders and allows developers to define actions before
attributes are collected from the user. For example, users can be blocked from signing
up based on their email or federated identity or some attribute values can be prefilled.
OnAttributeCollectionSubmit: This event is triggered when the user submits the
attributes collection form. It can be used to validate the user input. For example, you
can validate a customer number or invitation code. You can show a validation error
based on submitted values or block the user from signing up.
EmailOtpSend: When users receive OTP during sign-up or when they reset their
passwords, they receive emails in the default Microsoft format. Very little branding idx_00ac2101 and
customization is possible. It uses Microsoft gateway to send the emails. EmailOtpSend
allows organizations to call a REST API and use their own email providers for sending
OTPs.
TokenIssuanceStart: This is a custom claims provider that allows developers to inject
custom logic at the beginning of the token issuance process, right before the security
token is generated and returned to the user after successful authentication. This
extension can be used to perform additional validation, modify claims, or integrate
with external systems to enforce custom policies. By leveraging TokenIssuanceStart,
organizations can tailor the authentication and authorization experience, ensuring
that issued tokens meet specific business or security requirements before users gain
access to protected resources. You can call an external REST API to retrieve additional
user attributes, such as a user's dietary preference or location, and then configure
claims mapping to include those attributes as custom claims in the issued token. This
allows your application to use information from external systems during
authentication, ensuring tokens contain up-to-date and relevant user data.
These events can be created in the Microsoft Entra portal by navigating to Entra ID | External
identities | Custom authentication extensions | Create custom authentication extension.
They can then be injected in the user flow by navigating to Entra ID | External identities |
User flows. Select the user flow and click Custom authentication extensions. Choose if you
would like to idx_ed5c7a6e trigger the extension before collecting information from the user or after the user
submits their information.

Securing external tenants
Microsoft Entra External ID provides some baseline features in external tenants to protect
against threats idx_47820cbf like brute force and network layer attacks. These default settings provide a
foundation for developing a security plan for your external identities. The following built-in
security features are enabled by default in all external tenants to protect your applications
from threats.
Brute force protection: External tenants use Microsoft Entra ID's smart lockout
feature to prevent unauthorized access through repeated password guessing. Smart
lockout helps block out bad actors that try to guess a user's password or use brute-
force mechanisms. It can recognize attempts from bad actors and block them, while
letting legitimate users sign in.
Common networking HTTP Protection: This provides protection against network-
layer and timing-based attacks to protect against attempts to overwhelm resources and
make them inaccessible to users.
Account protection: Account protection helps safeguard user accounts from
unauthorized access to protect user data and prevent account breaches. Microsoft
offers integration with partner solutions like Akamai and Cloudflare for account
protection. These solutions are available in the Microsoft Entra portal by navigating to
Entra ID | Security Store | Protect apps from DDOS with WAF.
Access control: External ID uses role-based access control to ensure that only
authorized users get access to sensitive data. This is done using App roles and Groups.
Microsoft Entra ID allows you to define roles for your applications and assign users to
those roles. These roles then define the level of access users get in the application. Entra
ID sends the role information to the application as a claim in the user's security token.
Developers can also use Entra ID groups to define the level of access users have in the
application or to define which group gets access to which application. The group claim
is included in the user's security token.
Conditional Access policies: Conditional Access policies can be created in the external
tenant to trigger MFA, force a secure password reset or block access depending on
conditions like location or device platform and the application being accessed.
Multifactor authentication: MFA can be enforced to ensure that the legitimate user is
accessing the application. External tenants support Email and SMS OTP MFA. SMS

MFA automatically checks for fraud and prompts users to complete a CAPTCHA if fraud
is suspected. It also protects against telephony fraud. SMS is an add-on feature idx_c2537564 and
charged per SMS sent. MFA is implemented using Conditional Access policies.
Fraud protection: Consumer applications are prone to bot attacks and fake sign-ups.
Microsoft offers partner solutions like HUMAN and Arkose Labs that help protect
against these types of attacks. These solutions are available in the Microsoft Entra
portal by navigating to Entra ID | Security Store | Sign-up protection.
Native authentication
The out of the box branding capabilities in Microsoft Entra ID offer limited customization
capabilities. Sometimes, organizations need to provide fully customized user experiences and
user journeys. Native idx_44b21a62 authentication in Microsoft Entra External ID enables developers to build
fully customized, in-app sign-in experiences for mobile and desktop applications. This
approach allows applications to directly collect user credentials and interact with Entra's
identity APIs, offering a seamless, branded experience that aligns with the app's native UI.
Native authentication supports two primary credential types: email with one-time passcode
(OTP) and email idx_d6df9724 with password (including self-service password reset). It is ideal for scenarios
where redirecting to a browser is not feasible or desirable—such as mobile-first consumer
apps, kiosk environments, or embedded systems—where maintaining a consistent, immersive
user experience is critical.
Native authentication idx_2e9ffe6b does not currently support social IdPs or federated identity providers. It
supports Single Sign-On (SSO) for embedded web views and email and SMS OTP as MFA
methods. It also requires developers to handle more of the authentication flow, including
secure credential collection and token management. Microsoft strongly idx_9073b331 recommends using the
Microsoft Authentication Library (MSAL) SDKs for supported platforms (Android, iOS/
macOS, React, Angular) to simplify implementation and ensure best practices.
To enable native authentication, administrators must allow public client flows and explicitly
enable native authentication in the app registration. Developers must also configure supported
challenge types to inform Entra which authentication methods the app supports.
Use native authentication when you need full control over the sign-in UI, especially in mobile
or desktop apps where browser redirects disrupt the user experience. It's best suited for
consumer-facing apps where branding and flow consistency are paramount and where SSO or
federated identity idx_3cc6d60c is not required. Native authentication offers a powerful option for crafting
tailored identity experiences—provided the development team is equipped to manage the

Migrating to Entra External ID
Most organizations will have a CIAM solution that they are currently using. This could be
Azure AD B2C or idx_434f75e9 other solutions. Organizations wanting to adopt Entra External ID would like
to do so without disrupting end user experience. Migration involves migrating user credentials
and data. Migration consists of three main steps.
Directory cleanup: Moving to another system is a good opportunity to clean up data.
Migrate only the data that is required. Identify stale accounts and exclude them from
the migration. Identify required user attributes and don't migrate the ones not
required. This makes the migration process smoother and ensures that the new system
is clean.
User data migration: This is the step where user accounts are created in Entra External
ID. This can be done manually or by importing the user accounts from the existing
system to Entra External ID. Set a random password for now. Users' passwords will be
updated as part of the password migration process.
Password migration: The next step is to migrate user passwords. There are two
approaches to password migration.
Self-service password reset: In this approach when the user accounts are
migrated, a temporary password is created for the users. When the users log in,
they are prompted to reset their passwords using the forgot password option.
This approach is simple to implement; however, it does require users to reset
their passwords which might be disruptive for some users and organizations may
not like this.
Just-in-time (JIT) migration: Organizations that don't want to make users reset
their password can utilize JIT migration. This allows users to use their existing
passwords once their accounts are migrated. JIT migration involves invoking a
custom API during the sign-in process to validate the user's credentials against
the legacy IdP using the onPasswordSubmit custom authentication extension.
This extension allows defining custom logic that idx_d311fe71 runs during the authentication
process. From a user's perspective, this process is seamless. The user enters their
password in the application login screen. Behind the scenes, their password is

Monitoring External ID
Entra External idx_55f0521b ID offers the following tools to monitor user activity:
User activity insights: This dashboard provides insights into user activity and their
interaction with the applications registered in the external tenant. Using this
dashboard you can track monthly active users, monitor new users added, analyze daily
and monthly application sign-ins and assess MFA success and failures. This dashboard
is available in your external tenant by navigating to Entra ID | Monitoring & health |
Usage & insights.
Sign-up logs: Entra External ID records all sign-ups, including successes and failures.
Using these logs, organizations can gain insight into the sign-up process to enhance
the sign-up experience and improve customer engagement. These logs show the
percentage of sign-ups that led to successful account creation and drop-off rates.
Sign-in logs: Using sign-in logs, administrators can find out how many users sign in
and use applications, any failed sign-ins, and the browsers or devices from which users
are signing in.
Audit logs: Audit logs record information about any changes to the tenant, such as the
creation of new users, applications or groups, password resets, and a lot more.
Provisioning logs: These record the activities performed by the provisioning service.
For example, users created or deleted in registered applications.
Azure Monitor: Logs from the external tenant can be sent to Azure Monitor and a Log
Analytics workspace from where they can be ingested in Microsoft Sentinel for security
monitoring.
Summary
This chapter was a deep dive into Microsoft's CIAM solution. You learned how to create and
customize an external tenant. You also learned how to configure different identity providers
and register OIDC and SAML applications. Lastly, you learned the different security options
available to secure your external tenant and the applications registered in it. This chapter also
covered how developers can build pixel-perfect applications for end users using native
authentication, migrating from an existing CIAM solution to External ID and how you can
monitor your External ID tenant. In the next chapter, you will learn about Microsoft's Secure
Services Edge solution.

Microsoft Entra Internet Access
Today's way of working has changed. People no longer work in traditional offices. They work
from anywhere, using any device and network. As workloads move to the cloud, organizations
need an identity-aware idx_f1d3056b cloud-delivered network perimeter. This is called Secure Service Edge
(SSE). It is an advanced, cloud-delivered security framework designed to address the evolving
needs of modern organizations. As businesses increasingly adopt remote work and cloud-
based applications, traditional network perimeters become less effective. SSE responds to this
shift by delivering security functions directly from the cloud, ensuring that users, devices, and
data remain protected no matter where they are located or what network idx_e738e905 they use. At its core,
SSE consolidates several idx_17b7eb12 critical security services—such as secure web gateways (SWG),
cloud access security brokers (CASB), and zero trust network access (ZTNA) —into a
unified, centrally idx_6b79d61a managed platform. This consolidation not only reduces the complexity of
managing multiple, disparate security tools but also enhances visibility and control for IT
administrators. By enforcing policies at the network edge, SSE helps organizations defend
against cyber threats, manage user access, prevent data loss, and maintain regulatory
compliance. SSE empowers organizations to adopt flexible, hybrid work models without
compromising security. Microsoft's implementation of SSE, known idx_091c026b as Global Secure Access
(GSA), further extends these capabilities idx_aa7250d1 by integrating with Microsoft Entra Internet Access

Secure Access (GSA) to describe idx_a7af1a1f the SSE solution. Built on the principles of Zero Trust, GSA
provides secure access to internet or private resources for any user or device from any network.

Microsoft Entra Internet Access and Private Access together with Microsoft Defender for Cloud
